title: Student identity exposed in transit via submitted identifiers
description: The flow carries the student id together with course and submission details. If the transmission is observable in transit, the student can be directly identified from the payload.
assumptions: Assumes the flow is not adequately protected in transit or is exposed to intermediaries/logging components.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for direct identification from data content; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Linkability of submissions across courses or sessions
description: The combination of student id, course, and repeated submission events can allow multiple submissions or portal interactions to be linked to the same student across time or contexts.
assumptions: Assumes observers or intermediaries can access payload or stable metadata for multiple transmissions.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability through repeated/stable identifiers; exact node id may differ in a specific LINDDUN Pro catalog.

title: Disclosure of assignment contents in transit
description: The uploaded work file may contain personal data, opinions, writing style, or other sensitive content. Exposure of the file while in transit would disclose information beyond what is necessary to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Assumes insufficient transport protection or exposure through network monitoring, proxies, or debug logging.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for information disclosure from data content in transit.

title: Disclosure through communication metadata
description: Even if the file content is protected, metadata such as the fact that a specific student is submitting to a particular course at a particular time can reveal behavioral information.
assumptions: Assumes metadata is visible to network observers, infrastructure operators, or logs.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for disclosure via metadata/traffic data; exact node id may vary.

title: Portal can later deny receipt details or student can be unable to prove submission
description: If the portal does not provide reliable evidence of receipt, timestamp, and file integrity, there may be insufficient privacy-preserving proof about what was submitted and when. This can harm the student's ability to contest claims while also creating disputes around submission events.
assumptions: Assumes missing or weak receipts, audit trails, or confirmation mechanisms.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation-related node id is an informed estimate; exact LINDDUN Pro numbering may differ.

title: Secondary use of submitted assignment data without student awareness
description: On receipt, the portal or its operators may use the uploaded file and associated identifiers for purposes beyond assignment handling, such as plagiarism-model training, analytics, profiling, or service improvement, without making this use transparent to the student.
assumptions: Assumes the destination processes data for additional purposes not clearly communicated at collection time.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of awareness/unawareness about downstream processing; exact node id may vary.

title: Submission data collected or reused beyond necessity or valid legal basis
description: The destination may collect more data than necessary for assignment submission, retain it too long, or reuse it incompatibly with the original educational purpose, creating non-compliance risk.
assumptions: Assumes inadequate purpose limitation, data minimization, retention control, or legal basis management at the portal.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for non-compliance/privacy requirement violations at the destination.

title: Destination links assignment submissions with broader student activity
description: Once received, the portal can correlate the submission with login history, grades, course participation, device/browser data, or other institutional records, enabling a richer profile of the student.
assumptions: Assumes the portal or connected systems have access to other student datasets and perform correlation.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability created by recipient-side correlation; exact node id may differ.

title: Destination identifies student from assignment content or metadata
description: Even if explicit identifiers were minimized, the portal can identify the student from account context, file metadata, writing style, or course/submission context.
assumptions: Assumes the destination has contextual data or technical means to associate the submission with a specific student.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for identification by the recipient using contextual or indirect identifiers.

title: Portal discloses student and role data beyond what is necessary for routing
description: The portal may send more personal data than needed to the assignment & grading service when routing requests, such as persistent student identifiers or detailed role information, creating unnecessary disclosure from the source.
assumptions: The grading service may only need a scoped pseudonymous identifier or minimal authorization attributes rather than the full student id and full role context.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id based on source-side over-sharing/minimization failure; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree label may vary.

title: Submission and grading traffic can link a student across courses or assignments
description: Data in transit contains student id, course, file reference, and role, which together can enable linking multiple submissions, grading events, or course activities to the same individual across contexts.
assumptions: The flow is observable to intermediaries, logs, or monitoring components, or the identifiers are stable across transactions.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for linkability via data attributes on the flow.

title: Student identity may be directly identifiable in transit
description: The transmitted student id may directly identify the student to any party able to inspect the flow or its logs, especially when combined with course information and role.
assumptions: Student id is directly identifying or readily resolvable to a person within the environment.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifiability from direct identifiers on the data flow.

title: Metadata about submissions reveals sensitive academic activity
description: Even if file contents are not sent on this flow, the file reference, course, timing, and requesting role can disclose that a specific student submitted work, requested grading, or interacted with a particular course at a particular time.
assumptions: Transport, API gateway, or application logs expose request metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure through metadata on the flow; exact subtree may differ.

title: Assignment service may expose submission data internally or through logs
description: On receipt, the assignment & grading service may log or store student id, course, file reference, and role in ways accessible to operators, developers, or other components that do not need the data, causing disclosure at the destination.
assumptions: P2 performs request logging, tracing, debugging, or broad internal sharing.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for destination-side disclosure via storage/logging or excessive internal access.

title: Assignment service can link student activity across assignments and courses
description: Because P2 receives stable student identifiers together with course and file references, it can correlate a student's submissions and grading interactions over time, increasing linkability at the destination.
assumptions: P2 stores historical requests or has access to multiple courses/assignments for the same student.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for recipient-side correlation/linking.

title: Data may be used for purposes beyond grading and submission handling
description: The assignment & grading service could repurpose received data for analytics, performance profiling, model training, or monitoring of student behavior beyond the user's expected purpose of submission and grading.
assumptions: Purpose limitation is not technically enforced or contractually constrained.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for destination-side unawareness/unexpected secondary use; exact subtree may vary.

title: Processing may exceed consent, notice, or educational privacy expectations
description: If students or staff were not adequately informed that their identifiers, course context, file references, and role data would be processed by this separate grading service, the destination's processing may be non-compliant with applicable privacy requirements or stated notices.
assumptions: P2 is a distinct service or processor and transparency, legal basis, or data processing terms may be incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-compliance due to insufficient notice/legal basis; exact node may differ by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Insufficient evidence of who initiated grading-related actions
description: If P2 does not preserve privacy-respecting but reliable evidence of whether the request came from a student, instructor, or other role, participants may later deny having initiated a submission or grading request, leading to disputes that can trigger excessive data retention or intrusive logging.
assumptions: The service relies on weak request provenance or ambiguous role assertions from P1.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation is less central for this flow; included because role-based requests may later be disputed. Node id is approximate.

title: Stored submissions can be linked across courses or over time via student identifier
description: The assignment store receives and stores the submitted file together with a student id, course, and submission time. This enables linking multiple submissions belonging to the same student across assignments, courses, or semesters, creating a richer profile of the student's academic activity than may be necessary for grading alone.
assumptions: DS1 retains records over time and permits queries or access patterns that use the student id or related metadata for correlation.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from general LINDDUN knowledge; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may differ.

title: Student identity is directly identifiable in stored assignment records
description: Because the grading service stores the assignment file with the student id, the stored record directly identifies the student associated with the submission. Anyone with access to the store or derived outputs can identify who submitted a particular assignment.
assumptions: Student id is directly identifying within the system or can readily be mapped to a named student.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for direct identifiability at the destination.

title: Submission metadata in transit can link student activity
description: The data flow carries student id, course, and submission time. Even aside from file contents, this metadata can be used to link a student's actions across submissions and infer patterns such as punctuality, workload, or participation.
assumptions: Flow metadata or payload is observable to components, logs, or intermediaries beyond the minimum necessary processing path.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability via data in transit; exact numbering may vary.

title: Submission time and course metadata expose student behavior
description: The flow reveals personal aspects of the student's behavior, such as when they submit work, which course they are enrolled in, and potentially work habits or deadline-related behavior. This constitutes disclosure of personal information beyond the assignment content itself.
assumptions: The flow is accessible to logs, monitoring systems, or intermediaries, or is insufficiently protected in transit.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure of personal data in transit; exact LINDDUN Pro node may differ.

title: Stored assignment files may disclose sensitive personal information
description: Assignment files may contain personal data, opinions, writing style, or special-category information depending on the assignment topic. Storing the file together with student id, course, and submission time increases the privacy impact if the store is accessed for purposes beyond grading or by unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Assignment content may include personal or sensitive information and DS1 stores both content and identifying metadata together.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an informed approximation for disclosure through storage/processing at destination.

title: Storage enables profiling or secondary use beyond students' expectations
description: Once submissions and associated metadata are stored centrally, they may be reused for plagiarism analytics, performance profiling, training datasets, or disciplinary investigations in ways students do not expect from the act of submitting coursework for grading.
assumptions: DS1 data may be retained and repurposed beyond the immediate grading purpose without clear limitation.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for unawareness/non-transparent secondary use; exact node numbering may differ.

title: Students may lack meaningful choice or consent over retention and reuse of submissions
description: The destination stores identified submissions and metadata as part of the educational workflow. Students may have little or no ability to object to retention duration, secondary analysis, or reuse of their submissions, creating a non-compliance risk if legal basis, transparency, minimization, or rights handling are inadequate.
assumptions: The system does not clearly communicate retention and reuse practices or provide mechanisms required by applicable privacy law/policy.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-compliance/privacy rights concerns at the destination.

title: Stored submission records can be used as evidence of student actions without adequate contestability
description: By storing the file with student id and submission time, the system creates records that may later be treated as proof that a student submitted or failed to submit work at a certain time. If provenance, clock accuracy, overwrite handling, or dispute mechanisms are weak, students may be unable to plausibly deny or contest incorrect records.
assumptions: Submission records may be relied upon in academic disputes or misconduct processes.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation-related privacy relevance is somewhat context-dependent here; node id is approximate.

title: Teacher identity disclosed by login/request data
description: When the teacher logs in and requests the review queue, the transmitted credentials or account identifiers can directly identify the teacher to the receiving system and any party able to observe the submission of the request.
assumptions: Assumes the request contains a username, email address, staff ID, session bootstrap token, or equivalent account-linked identifier.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is my best-fit estimate for direct identification via provided identity data; exact LINDDUN Pro numbering may differ.

title: Teacher activity can be linked across sessions via persistent identifiers
description: If the login/request flow carries stable identifiers such as account names, cookies, device identifiers, or long-lived tokens, observations of multiple requests can be linked to the same teacher over time, revealing patterns of grading activity.
assumptions: Assumes persistent identifiers or otherwise stable metadata are present on the flow and observable to the portal or intermediaries.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability through persistent identifiers in transit; numbering may be approximate.

title: Teacher login and review activity is detectable from traffic metadata
description: Even if message contents are protected, the existence, timing, frequency, source, destination, and size of requests may reveal that a specific teacher is accessing the grading queue, enabling inference about work schedules or course activity.
assumptions: Assumes network or application-layer metadata are observable by the portal, infrastructure operators, or attackers with traffic visibility.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for detectability from communication metadata; exact node id may vary.

title: Portal links teacher login with course and submission-review context
description: On receipt, the web app can associate the teacher's identity with the set of courses taught and the queue of submissions awaiting review, enabling broader profiling of the teacher's responsibilities and behavior across portal functions.
assumptions: Assumes the portal stores or correlates teacher account, course assignments, and queue-access events.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability caused by recipient-side correlation; exact numbering may differ.

title: Portal can infer sensitive aspects of teacher behavior from queue requests
description: By processing repeated queue requests, the portal can derive when the teacher is active, workload levels, turnaround habits, and possibly periods of absence or unusual behavior, beyond what is strictly necessary to serve the request.
assumptions: Assumes access events are logged or otherwise available for analytics or monitoring.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for recipient-side detectability/inference from observed behavior; exact node id may be approximate.

title: Teacher may be unaware of logging and secondary use of access events
description: If the portal does not clearly inform teachers that login and queue-access events are logged, analyzed, or reused for monitoring, performance management, or analytics, the teacher may be insufficiently aware of how their personal data are processed.
assumptions: Assumes notice is incomplete, unclear, or absent regarding logging and downstream uses of access-event data.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of awareness/transparency; exact node id may differ.

title: Queue-access data may be processed beyond necessity or without a valid basis
description: The portal may collect or retain more login/request data than necessary for authentication and queue retrieval, or reuse those data for unrelated analytics, monitoring, or profiling without an appropriate legal basis or policy justification.
assumptions: Assumes data minimization, purpose limitation, retention limits, or lawful-basis controls are weak or absent.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance with minimization/purpose-limitation obligations; exact node id may vary.

title: Teacher could later deny having accessed the review queue if evidence handling is weak
description: If authentication and audit records for the login/request are incomplete, mutable, or poorly bound to the teacher account, the teacher may be able to repudiate having accessed the submissions queue, creating disputes around accountability and the handling of personal data in logs.
assumptions: Assumes the system relies on access logs for accountability and those logs lack integrity protection or sufficient detail.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation is less central here than other privacy threats; included because access-event logging can create or fail to prevent repudiation. Node id is approximate.

title: Portal reveals directly identifying student information to the teacher
description: The web app displays student names alongside submissions and timestamps. This directly identifies the submitting students to the teacher through this disclosure.
assumptions: Assumes the teacher does not already know the identity of every submission or that identity revelation is broader than strictly necessary for the task.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best-fit estimate for direct identification by content disclosure.

title: Teacher can link multiple submissions and activities to the same student
description: Because the portal shows student names together with work content and submission times, the teacher can link multiple submissions, timing patterns, and possibly behavior across assignments to the same student.
assumptions: Assumes the portal presents persistent identifiers such as names across multiple submissions or assignments.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability via persistent identifiers; exact subtree may vary by catalog version.

title: Work content may disclose sensitive personal information about students
description: Student submission content itself may contain personal, special-category, or otherwise sensitive information. Displaying full work content to the teacher may disclose more personal information than necessary for grading or review.
assumptions: Assumes some submissions can contain personal reflections, health details, family circumstances, or other sensitive content.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate because the exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for content-based disclosure of sensitive attributes may differ.

title: Submission metadata in transit can identify students or teachers
description: Even if transport content is protected, metadata on the flow such as session identifiers, endpoints, timing, and access patterns may allow identification of the teacher reviewing specific student submissions or of the students whose records are being accessed.
assumptions: Assumes observable network or application-layer metadata is available to an attacker or intermediary.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifiability from communication metadata; exact node may differ.

title: Teacher can later deny having viewed specific submissions
description: If the destination side does not maintain adequate viewing or access logs, the teacher may be able to deny having accessed particular student submissions or timestamps, reducing accountability for privacy-relevant access.
assumptions: Assumes access logging, audit trails, or acknowledgements are absent or insufficient at the recipient side.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate for non-repudiation failure related to receipt/access of data.

title: Teacher may use submission data beyond the students' expected purpose
description: After receiving names, work content, and submission times, the teacher could use the information for purposes beyond grading or feedback, such as profiling punctuality, inferring personal circumstances, or sharing details with others.
assumptions: Assumes purpose limitation is not technically or organizationally enforced at the destination.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for unauthorized or unexpected secondary use; exact subtree may vary.

title: Students may not be adequately informed that teachers can view detailed submission metadata
description: If students are not clearly informed that teachers will see not only their work but also names and precise submission times, the disclosure may occur without sufficient transparency or valid consent/notice where required.
assumptions: Assumes the system lacks clear privacy notice or another valid legal basis/expectation covering this visibility.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate because non-compliance depends on the applicable legal basis and notice obligations.

title: Student identified in transit via student ID
description: The flow carries a student identifier alongside grade and feedback. If the transmission is observed or insufficiently protected, the student can be directly identified from the data in transit.
assumptions: Assumes the student ID is unique and meaningful to the recipient or an interceptor.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is best-effort; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may differ.

title: Linkability of grading events across submissions
description: The combination of student ID, grader ID, grade, and feedback metadata can allow multiple grading events to be linked to the same student and teacher, revealing patterns such as teacher grading behavior or a student's performance history.
assumptions: Assumes repeated observations of this flow or access to correlated records/metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection; exact subnode may differ depending on the threat tree version.

title: Disclosure of confidential educational data in transit
description: Grades and written feedback are sensitive educational records. If the flow is intercepted, logged insecurely, or exposed through transport-layer weaknesses, confidential information about the student may be disclosed.
assumptions: Assumes transport or intermediary logging may be accessible to unauthorized parties.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of grades and feedback at the portal
description: Upon receipt, the web app may store or expose grades, feedback text, student ID, and grader ID to unauthorized users, administrators, or connected components if access control is insufficient.
assumptions: Assumes the portal persists or further processes the submitted data.
uncertainty_note: Exact LINDDUN Pro node id may differ.

title: Linking teacher and student profiles through stored grading records
description: The destination can combine grader ID and student ID across many submissions, enabling linkage between teachers, students, courses, and performance records beyond what data subjects may expect.
assumptions: Assumes the portal aggregates records over time.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id.

title: Teacher cannot plausibly deny having submitted a grade entry
description: If the portal logs the grader ID, timestamp, and submission details, the teacher may be unable to deny having recorded a specific grade or feedback entry. This can be a privacy concern where detailed action logs are retained or broadly accessible.
assumptions: Assumes the system creates attributable audit logs tied to the teacher identity.
uncertainty_note: Applicability depends on whether non-repudiation is considered undesirable in this context; node id approximate.

title: Unawareness about secondary use or retention of grading data
description: Teachers and students may be unaware that submitted grades and feedback are retained, analyzed, reused for performance analytics, or shared with other school systems after receipt by the portal.
assumptions: Assumes insufficient notice or transparency about downstream processing.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate.

title: Processing grades and feedback beyond educational purpose or legal basis
description: The portal may process or retain grade and feedback data in ways that are excessive, incompatible with the original educational purpose, or not aligned with applicable privacy obligations, such as using feedback text for unrelated analytics.
assumptions: Assumes governance or purpose-limitation controls may be weak.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id may differ; compliance assessment depends on jurisdiction and policy.

title: Excessive disclosure of grade-record attributes to the database
description: The grading service writes a full grade record including student id, course, grade, feedback, grader id, and timestamp. If all fields are not necessary for the intended storage purpose, the source discloses more personal data than needed, increasing privacy impact.
assumptions: Assumes some fields (for example detailed feedback, grader id, or precise timestamp) may not be strictly necessary for all downstream purposes or could be stored separately/minimized.
uncertainty_note: Node id is my best-fit estimate for disclosure due to oversharing/minimization at the source; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree label may differ.

title: Identification of the student from data in transit
description: The flow contains a direct student identifier together with course and grade information. Any party able to observe the transmission can identify the student associated with the grade record.
assumptions: Assumes the flow could be observed by an unauthorized party due to insufficient transport protection, logging, or monitoring exposure.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for direct identification from transmitted content; exact node numbering may vary.

title: Linkability of student academic events across records
description: Student id, course, grader id, and timestamp enable linking this write event with other grade submissions, course participation records, audit logs, or academic history, allowing construction of a richer profile of the student and grading activity.
assumptions: Assumes repeated use of stable identifiers and accessible correlated datasets or logs.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability via stable identifiers and metadata on the flow.

title: Disclosure of sensitive academic performance data in transit
description: The transmitted grade, feedback, and associated metadata reveal sensitive educational information. Interception or unintended exposure of the flow would disclose confidential student performance details and potentially staff-related information via grader id.
assumptions: Assumes inadequate encryption, exposed middleware, verbose message tracing, or unauthorized access to network/application logs.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for confidentiality loss of personal data on the flow; exact subtree id may differ.

title: Linkability through centralized storage of grade records
description: The database can link grade records across courses, terms, and instructors using student id, grader id, and timestamps, enabling broad profiling of a student's academic trajectory and staff grading patterns.
assumptions: Assumes DS2 stores multiple records over time and supports queries or joins across datasets.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability caused by recipient-side storage and correlation.

title: Identification through stored grade records
description: Because the database stores direct identifiers with grades and feedback, anyone with access to the datastore can identify the student and grader associated with each record.
assumptions: Assumes access controls, segregation, or pseudonymization may be insufficient for all access paths such as admins, analysts, backups, or replicas.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for identification at the destination due to stored direct identifiers.

title: Unauthorized disclosure from stored grade records
description: The destination stores highly sensitive educational records. Misconfigured access control, excessive retention, insecure backups, replication, or secondary use could disclose grades, feedback, and grader information to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Assumes DS2 may expose data through operational copies, reporting interfaces, or insider access beyond the original grading purpose.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for disclosure at rest / on receipt; exact numbering may differ.

title: Unawareness of storage and secondary use of grading data
description: Students and possibly graders may be unaware that detailed feedback, grader id, and timestamps are stored in the grade records database, how long they are retained, who can access them, and whether they are reused for analytics, audits, or performance monitoring.
assumptions: Assumes transparency notices or role-specific privacy information are incomplete or not effectively communicated.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of transparency/unawareness at the destination.

title: Non-compliance with data minimization, purpose limitation, or retention obligations
description: Storing the full grade record with detailed feedback, grader id, and precise timestamp in a central database may exceed what is necessary for the stated educational purpose or may be retained longer than permitted by policy or law.
assumptions: Assumes applicable institutional policy or legal obligations require minimization, defined retention, access restriction, or separation of duties for educational records.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for compliance failures at the destination; exact node id may differ.

title: Linkability of repeated grade-access requests via network metadata
description: Repeated requests by the same student to view grades/feedback may be linkable through stable identifiers or metadata on the flow, such as session cookies, IP address, device fingerprints, or timing patterns, allowing correlation of multiple accesses to the same individual.
assumptions: The web app uses persistent sessions or other request metadata that can correlate multiple requests over time.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from general LINDDUN Pro knowledge; exact subtree label may vary.

title: Identifiability of the student from request contents or metadata
description: The request may directly or indirectly identify the student through login credentials, student number, email address, IP address, or other metadata transmitted with the request, enabling recognition of the requester as a specific person.
assumptions: The student is authenticated or otherwise provides identifiers when requesting grades.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for identifiability from data/metadata in transit.

title: Disclosure by the student of more personal data than necessary in the request
description: The student may include unnecessary personal information in free-text fields, support messages, or request parameters when asking for grades/feedback, causing excessive disclosure at the moment of sharing.
assumptions: The request interface allows entry of free text or optional fields beyond what is strictly needed to retrieve grades.
uncertainty_note: Applies only if the request mechanism permits optional or free-form input; node id is approximate.

title: Unnecessary collection or retention of request metadata by the portal
description: On receipt of the request, the grades portal may log or retain more personal data than necessary, such as detailed access logs, device information, location inference, or full request contents, increasing disclosure risk.
assumptions: The portal stores access logs or analytics data associated with grade-view requests.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure subtree node based on over-collection/retention at the destination.

title: Unawareness of logging or secondary use of grade-access requests
description: The student may be unaware that their request to view grades and feedback is logged, profiled, monitored for analytics, or reused for purposes beyond delivering the requested information.
assumptions: The portal provides limited transparency about monitoring, analytics, or retention practices.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id may differ depending on the LINDDUN Pro version; threat applicability is strong.

title: Non-compliance if the portal processes request data without a valid privacy basis or adequate minimization
description: If the portal collects, logs, or reuses personal data from grade-access requests beyond what is necessary for providing the service, it may violate privacy obligations such as purpose limitation, data minimization, transparency, or retention constraints.
assumptions: Applicable where institutional policy or privacy law constrains processing of student access data.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance depends on the governing legal/policy context; node id is best-fit.

title: Excessive disclosure of grades or feedback beyond what is necessary
description: The portal may display more academic information than needed for the student's immediate purpose, such as historical grades, internal assessment notes, or detailed teacher feedback that was not intended for student view.
assumptions: Assumes the web app may expose more fields than necessary in the UI or response payload.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best-fit estimate for disclosure through oversharing by the source process.

title: Student identity revealed through the content delivered
description: The displayed grades and feedback inherently identify the student to whom they relate. If the app renders this data in a context visible to others, the student's identity can be inferred from the content.
assumptions: Assumes shoulder surfing, shared devices, or visible browser sessions are plausible in the usage context.
uncertainty_note: Identification is somewhat contextual here because the data is intentionally shown to the student; the threat materializes if others can observe it.

title: Linkability via network metadata for repeated grade-viewing sessions
description: Even if transport encryption protects content, metadata on the flow such as timing, endpoint, session identifiers, or repeated access patterns may allow an observer to link multiple grade-viewing events to the same student or household.
assumptions: Assumes an attacker can observe traffic metadata or logs associated with this flow.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability from data-flow metadata; exact node may vary by threat-tree version.

title: Disclosure of grades and feedback in transit
description: If the flow is not adequately protected in transit, grades and teacher feedback could be intercepted by an unauthorized party, exposing sensitive educational information.
assumptions: Assumes weak or absent transport protection, misconfiguration, or interception on an untrusted network.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an estimated best fit for disclosure during transmission.

title: Disclosure to others at the student's endpoint
description: Once received, the grades and feedback may be exposed on the student's device to family members, peers, or others through shared devices, screenshots, browser caching, notifications, or unattended sessions.
assumptions: Assumes the student uses a shared or insufficiently protected endpoint.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure arising at the recipient side after receipt.

title: Student can deny having received or viewed the grades and feedback
description: If the system lacks reliable evidence of presentation or access, the student may later dispute having seen the grades or teacher feedback, which can affect accountability around acknowledgements or follow-up actions.
assumptions: Relevant only if the organization relies on portal display as evidence that information was communicated.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation is somewhat context-dependent because simple viewing may not require non-repudiation in all educational settings.

title: Parent identity may be exposed on the login/request flow
description: Credentials, session identifiers, or request contents sent from the parent to the grades portal could directly identify the parent if intercepted or insufficiently protected in transit.
assumptions: Assumes the flow carries login credentials and/or authenticated requests over a network path where transport protection could fail or be downgraded.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may differ.

title: Parent-child relationship may be linkable from traffic or request metadata
description: The request to view a child's grades inherently encodes that the parent account is linked to a specific child account. Observing message contents or metadata could allow linking the parent to the child and to repeated grade-access events.
assumptions: Assumes identifiers for both parent and child, or stable account/session metadata, are present or inferable in the flow.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an approximate best fit from memory.

title: Portal can infer sensitive facts about family relationship and student status
description: By receiving the login and grade request, the portal learns that this parent is associated with a particular child and is seeking that child's academic records, revealing family linkage and educational context beyond mere authentication.
assumptions: Assumes the portal stores or can inspect the parent-child account linkage and request purpose.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit detectability node id from memory; exact numbering may vary.

title: Parent may be unaware of how access requests are logged and used
description: The web app may log parent login attempts and grade-access requests for analytics, monitoring, or secondary purposes without the parent fully understanding this processing.
assumptions: Assumes privacy notices or just-in-time explanations are incomplete or not salient.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node id from memory.

title: Insufficient consent or authorization basis for linked-account grade access
description: If the portal does not properly verify that the parent is authorized to access this specific child's grades, the processing may occur without valid consent, legal authority, or policy-compliant parental linkage.
assumptions: Assumes parental linkage or guardianship status may be stale, incorrect, or insufficiently validated.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node id from memory.

title: Parent may later be unable to deny having requested the grades
description: If the portal keeps strong authentication and access logs tied to the parent account, those records can be used to prove that the parent initiated the grade request, reducing plausible deniability.
assumptions: Assumes detailed audit logging is retained and attributable to the parent account.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate from memory; repudiation-related numbering may differ.

title: Excessive disclosure of student educational records to the parent
description: The portal may disclose more of the child's educational record than is necessary for the parent's purpose, such as detailed feedback, full submission history, or grades beyond the relevant period, increasing privacy impact on the child.
assumptions: Assumes the parent does not always need the full historical record and that data minimization is expected for this context.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id based on over-disclosure/data minimization at the source; exact LINDDUN Pro node wording may differ.

title: Identification of the child through displayed academic records
description: The shared grades, teacher feedback, and submission history directly identify the child to the recipient and may expose the child's academic profile in a personally attributable way.
assumptions: Assumes the portal content is tied to a specific child account and contains directly attributable educational information.
uncertainty_note: Identification is inherent in this flow; node id is a best-fit estimate.

title: Linkability of parent and child via portal traffic metadata
description: Even if transport is protected, traffic metadata or observable communication patterns may allow an observer to link a specific parent to a specific student account or school relationship.
assumptions: Assumes some metadata is observable to network or infrastructure observers.
uncertainty_note: Applies mainly where metadata is exposed; exact node id may differ in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Disclosure of grades and feedback in transit
description: If the flow is insufficiently protected in transit, grades, feedback, and submission history could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, revealing sensitive educational information.
assumptions: Assumes transport security could be absent, weak, or misconfigured.
uncertainty_note: Classic in-transit confidentiality threat; node id is best-fit.

title: Further disclosure by the parent to unauthorized third parties
description: After receiving the child's grades and feedback, the parent may intentionally or accidentally share screenshots, printouts, or verbal summaries with others who are not authorized to access the child's educational information.
assumptions: Assumes the parent can store, copy, or redistribute the received information.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit destination-side disclosure/storage-sharing node; exact node id may vary.

title: Unawareness by the child about parental access to detailed academic history
description: The child may be unaware of the extent, granularity, or timing of what is shown to the parent, including detailed feedback and submission history, reducing transparency about personal-data sharing.
assumptions: Assumes the child is a data subject distinct from the parent and is not clearly informed about this disclosure.
uncertainty_note: Unawareness is centered on the data subject affected by this recipient-side access; node id is approximate.

title: Sharing educational data without appropriate legal basis or consent handling
description: Displaying the child's grades, feedback, and submission history to the parent may violate privacy obligations if the portal does not correctly account for custody status, age of the student, local education/privacy law, or consent/authorization requirements.
assumptions: Assumes legal entitlement to parental access can vary by jurisdiction and student circumstances.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance applicability depends strongly on jurisdiction and school policy; node id is best-fit.

title: Administrator shares excessive account and relationship data
description: The school administrator may submit more personal data than necessary when creating or modifying accounts and parent-child links, such as unnecessary names, emails, roles, or relationship attributes, causing disclosure at the moment of sharing.
assumptions: The portal may not enforce strict data minimization on account-management forms.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for unnecessary disclosure by oversharing; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary.

title: Linkability via account-management transaction metadata
description: Even if payload contents are protected, metadata on this flow can reveal that a specific administrator is creating, modifying, or disabling accounts and parent-child links, allowing correlation of administrative actions over time and linking affected students, parents, or staff records.
assumptions: An observer can access network metadata, logs, or message traces associated with this flow.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for linkability from communication metadata.

title: Identifiability of individuals from data in transit
description: Names, emails, roles, and parent-child relationship data transmitted on this flow can directly identify administrators, parents, and students if intercepted or exposed in transit.
assumptions: Transport protection may be absent, weak, terminated in an untrusted zone, or logs may capture payloads.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for direct identifiability from transmitted personal data.

title: Disclosure of sensitive relationship information in transit
description: Parent-child links and account status changes can disclose confidential family relationship information and administrative actions if the flow is intercepted, logged, or exposed to intermediaries.
assumptions: Relationship data is considered sensitive in context and may traverse components that can inspect or retain it.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure of personal/relationship data on the flow.

title: Portal links identities and relationships across accounts
description: On receipt, the grades portal can correlate administrator actions, user accounts, roles, and parent-child links across multiple records, enabling broad linkage of family and school identities beyond what each data subject expects.
assumptions: The portal stores and indexes account and relationship data centrally.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability caused by recipient-side correlation/storage.

title: Portal makes individuals identifiable through centralized account records
description: By storing names, emails, roles, and family relationships together, the portal enables straightforward identification of students, parents, and administrators, including inference of who belongs to which family.
assumptions: The portal retains these attributes in identifiable form.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifiability arising at the destination through storage/processing.

title: Insufficient evidence of administrative changes
description: If the portal does not maintain trustworthy audit trails for account creation, modification, disabling, and parent-child link changes, administrators may later be unable to prove or disprove having performed specific actions affecting individuals.
assumptions: Audit logging, integrity protection, or attribution controls may be incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-repudiation issues at the recipient; exact subtree may differ.

title: Portal stores more account and family data than necessary
description: The grades portal may retain unnecessary personal data or preserve obsolete parent-child links and disabled-account details longer than needed, increasing disclosure risk to students, parents, and staff.
assumptions: Retention and minimization controls may be weak or undefined.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for destination-side disclosure due to excessive retention/processing.

title: Data subjects may be unaware of account-link management processing
description: Parents, students, or staff may not be aware that administrators can create, modify, disable accounts, and establish or remove parent-child links in the portal, reducing transparency about how their relationship data is processed.
assumptions: Notices or in-product explanations to affected users may be limited.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of awareness/transparency at the destination.

title: Account and relationship management may exceed stated purpose or legal basis
description: If the portal processes names, emails, roles, and parent-child links for purposes beyond school administration, or without an appropriate legal basis and policy alignment, the processing may be non-compliant with privacy obligations.
assumptions: Purpose limitation, legal basis, and governance constraints are relevant and may not be fully enforced.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for destination-side non-compliance; exact node may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Linkability through persistent parent-child relationship records
description: The account directory can link student account records with parent/guardian accounts via stored relationship links, enabling correlation of identities and activities across family members and over time.
assumptions: DS3 stores persistent identifiers for both parties and retains explicit relationship mappings.

title: Identifiability of students and parents in directory records
description: Writing account records into the directory may make students and parents directly identifiable through names, usernames, email addresses, account IDs, or other unique attributes stored together.
assumptions: Account records contain direct identifiers or combinations of attributes sufficient to single out individuals.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for direct identifiability from stored identifiers.

title: Detectability of family association from directory presence
description: The mere presence of a parent-child relationship entry in the account directory may reveal that a given student has an associated parent/guardian account, even if full record contents are not exposed.
assumptions: Attackers or unauthorized internal users can observe existence of records, indexes, or lookup results in DS3.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for detectability based on existence of stored records rather than full content disclosure.

title: Disclosure of sensitive relationship data in the directory
description: The account directory stores parent-child links, which disclose personal relationship information and potentially educational context if accessed beyond what is necessary.
assumptions: Relationship links are accessible to components, administrators, or users beyond the minimum necessary audience.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure of stored relationship attributes; exact subtree may differ.

title: Excessive sharing of account and relationship data to the directory
description: The grading service may write more account attributes or relationship details than are necessary for directory purposes, creating a privacy risk due to non-compliant or non-minimized processing.
assumptions: P2 has access to richer student/family data than DS3 strictly needs for account-directory functions.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-compliance/data minimization concerns at the source.

title: Unawareness of secondary use of relationship records
description: Students and parents may be unaware that relationship links written for grading-related operations are stored in the account directory and could later be reused for authentication, communications, analytics, or administrative purposes.
assumptions: Notices or interfaces do not clearly explain this storage and reuse of relationship data.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for data subjects being unaware of storage and downstream use.

title: Excessive disclosure through full backup replication
description: The source process sends full grade records, assignments, and the account directory to the cloud hosting provider as part of nightly backup/replication. Replicating the entire dataset may disclose more personal data than is necessary for the hosting purpose, including sensitive educational records and directory information.
assumptions: Assumes the cloud provider does not need unrestricted access to all fields in identifiable form for every backup/replication operation.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best-fit estimate for over-disclosure/data minimization failure at the source.

title: Linkability created by consolidated full-record transfer
description: Sending complete grade records, assignments, and account directory entries together enables the recipient to link academic performance, coursework, and identity/account information belonging to the same individuals across contexts and over time.
assumptions: Assumes the datasets could otherwise be separated, pseudonymized, or access-segmented to reduce cross-context linkage.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; best-fit for source-side creation of linkability by sharing correlated datasets.

title: Identifiability from account directory and educational records
description: The replicated backup includes account directory data alongside grades and assignments, making students and staff directly identifiable to the cloud provider or anyone with access there.
assumptions: Assumes account directory contains direct identifiers such as names, usernames, email addresses, or institutional IDs.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; best-fit for source-side disclosure of directly identifying data.

title: Linkability via transfer metadata
description: Even if payload protections exist, recurring nightly replication may expose metadata such as timing, volume, endpoints, tenant identifiers, or routing information that can be used to link the education service with specific organizational units or user populations over time.
assumptions: Assumes some network, platform, or operational metadata is observable to intermediaries or the provider.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; best-fit for data-flow-level metadata-based linkability.

title: Identifiability via data-in-transit metadata or insufficient transport protection
description: If transport metadata or payload contents are exposed during replication, individuals represented in the backup may become identifiable in transit through visible identifiers, filenames, object names, or unprotected content.
assumptions: Assumes transport or storage-transfer mechanisms may reveal identifiers in metadata or may be misconfigured.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; best-fit for flow-level identifiability in transit.

title: Secondary use or over-access by cloud hosting provider
description: Upon receipt, the cloud hosting provider may process, inspect, index, or make the replicated educational records accessible to personnel or subprocessors beyond what is necessary for hosting and backup, causing disclosure to additional parties.
assumptions: Assumes provider-side operational access, support access, or subprocessor involvement is possible.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is approximate; best-fit for destination-side disclosure/overexposure.

title: Unawareness of third-party replication and provider-side processing
description: Students and staff may be unaware that their full assignments, grades, and directory data are replicated nightly to an external cloud provider, including any provider-side storage locations, retention, support access, or subprocessing.
assumptions: Assumes notices are incomplete or not sufficiently specific about third-party backup/replication practices.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; best-fit for lack of data subject awareness regarding destination-side processing.

title: Non-compliance risk from cross-border storage, retention, or contractual mismatch
description: The cloud provider's backup/replication environment may store educational records in jurisdictions, retention regimes, or contractual arrangements that do not meet applicable privacy obligations for student data, creating compliance risk.
assumptions: Assumes educational records are subject to legal, contractual, or policy restrictions on location, retention, access, or processor terms.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; best-fit for destination-side compliance failure.

title: Insufficient provability of provider actions on replicated data
description: If the cloud provider lacks auditable records for access, restoration tests, support handling, deletion, or subprocessor transfers involving the replicated backups, it may be difficult to prove what happened to individuals' data.
assumptions: Assumes audit logging, evidence retention, or contractual transparency may be incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; best-fit for destination-side non-repudiation/provability gap.

title: Cross-role linkage of grade records across student, parent, and teacher views
description: The grading service reads the same grade records to construct multiple role-specific views. If identifiers or stable record keys are reused internally, P2 can link a student's performance data across contexts and audiences, enabling broader profiling of the student and relationships among student, parent, and teacher.
assumptions: P2 has access to identifiers or quasi-identifiers that persist across the different views or sessions.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability due to correlating records across contexts; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary.

title: Identification of students or parents from grade records
description: Grade records are typically directly identifying or easily attributable when combined with class, assignment, or relationship information. On receipt, the grading service may identify specific students and infer associated parents and teachers from the records used to build views.
assumptions: Grade records include names, student IDs, class membership, parent relationships, or other strong identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for identifiability from received content.

title: Excessive disclosure of grade details to role-specific views
description: Because P2 builds student, parent, and teacher views from the same underlying records, it may expose more grade detail than necessary for a given role, such as teacher-only annotations appearing in parent or student views, or unnecessary historical performance data being shown.
assumptions: Role-based filtering or field-level access control may be incomplete or misconfigured in P2.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node for overexposure at the destination; exact subtree may differ.

title: Unawareness of secondary use of grade records for multiple audiences
description: Students and parents may be unaware that the grading service repurposes stored grade records to generate several distinct views and potentially derive summaries, trends, or contextual information beyond the original recording of grades.
assumptions: Notices do not clearly explain all downstream uses of grade records within the service.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit detectability/unawareness-related node; exact LINDDUN Pro mapping may vary.

title: Insufficient transparency about how grade data is processed in views
description: The grading service may not make it clear to students, parents, or teachers which grade attributes are used, how views are generated, or why certain information is visible to one role but not another, reducing users' awareness and ability to understand processing.
assumptions: The system lacks clear explanations, audit visibility, or contextual notices for role-based view generation.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of transparency/awareness; exact subtree may differ.

title: Processing of grade records beyond consent, expectation, or policy constraints
description: If grade records are reused by P2 for audiences or purposes not covered by consent, school policy, or applicable educational privacy obligations, the destination processing may be non-compliant, especially where parent access depends on student age or legal status.
assumptions: Applicable policy or legal constraints limit which grade information may be shown to which role and under what conditions.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node; exact node id depends on the applicable compliance basis.

title: Identification through metadata on the database-to-service read flow
description: Even if payload protections exist, metadata on the read flow—such as record keys, query parameters, class identifiers, or timing—may identify a specific student, assignment, or teacher relationship in transit between DS2 and P2.
assumptions: Flow metadata is observable within the environment or logged by intermediaries.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for identifiability from data-flow metadata; exact subtree may vary.

title: Linkability via repeated access patterns on grade-record reads
description: Repeated reads from the grade database to the grading service can create observable patterns that link requests to particular students, classes, or grading events. An observer or intermediary could correlate these accesses over time to build profiles of academic activity.
assumptions: Access patterns, timestamps, or query structures are visible to logs, monitoring systems, or network observers.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability from flow metadata and repeated interactions.
